name: ledger
description: Accounts, transfers, interest, fees and monthly statements for a small credit union.
author: test-split author (Claude, independent of the reviewer code)

issues.description: withdraw compares the amount with the balance alone, so a checking account can never use its overdraft limit, contrary to the docstring (transfer correctly uses can_debit).
issues.fix_hint: Refuse only when not account.can_debit(value), i.e. compare with balance plus overdraft limit.

issues.description: quantize without a rounding mode uses the context default ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so 1.125 becomes 1.12; the docstring and README say amounts are rounded half up.
Only the source account is checked for being open; money can be transferred into a closed account although the docstring says both accounts must be open.
issues.fix_hint: Load the target with _open_account so a closed target raises AccountClosed.

issues.description: The owner name is put into the SQL text with an f-string, so a crafted name ("x' OR '1'='1") returns every account.
issues.fix_hint: Use a ? placeholder and pass owner as a parameter.

issues.description: The SQLite storage layer imports the fee and interest policies and runs the month-end process itself (post_month_end); persistence depends on business rules instead of a service module using the store.

issues.anchor: def month_range(year: int, month: int) -> tuple[date, date]:
issues.description: The first/last day of a month helper is written twice, fees.month_range and statements._month_bounds.
if / for / if / if / if nested five levels deep; guard clauses and a filtered count would flatten it.

decoys.why_it_is_fine: The f-string only inserts a list of ? placeholders; every account id and date is passed as a query parameter.
md5 is used as a document fingerprint for look-up, not for security, and changing it would break matching statements already sent.
